# comma-residue-lab

Public execution artifact of a domain-general computational methodology applied to a previously unseen problem domain.

**Domain**: multiplicative interval closure under the free abelian group generated by octave (2/1) and fifth (3/2), and the residual obstruction (Pythagorean comma) that appears on the classical 12-fifth identification.

**Process enforced and recorded**:

1. RESTRICT  — hard bounds and refusals  
2. REPRESENT — free group + log-frequency embedding  
3. CONSTRUCT — naive stack of fifths + explicit hypothesis H0  
4. MEASURE   — residual quantified; H0 rejected  
5. RESOLVE   — pure residual kept; tempered fifth derived in parallel  
6. V&V       — independent numerical checks  
7. CERTIFY   — two coexisting certified objects; negative results preserved  

The test is whether an independent observer can watch a previously unseen problem become a constrained computational object, watch the system discover and correct its own errors, and determine from the repository that the same underlying methodology generated the solution.

No domain-specific templates from prior repositories were used. Failed hypotheses and residue remain in the tree.

```bash
python -m src.run_all   # or from src/ : python run_all.py
```

See CERTIFY.md for the final ledger.
